question.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨\frac{4}{3}(1+t)^{3/2},\,t,\,\frac{4}{3}(1-t)^{3/2}⟩,$ $-1\le t\le 1,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=3t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
question.worked_solution:
First, since $s=3t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{3}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{3}) \\  & =⟨\frac{4}{3}{(1+\frac{s}{3})}^{3/2},\,\frac{s}{3},\,\frac{4}{3}{(1-\frac{s}{3})}^{3/2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parameterized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{3}{(1+\frac{s}{3})}^{3/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s}{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{3}{(1+\frac{s}{3})}^{3/2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{1+\frac{s}{3}},\,\frac{1}{3},\,-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{1-\frac{s}{3}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}⟨\sqrt{3+s},\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\sqrt{3-s}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
